query: Which material can be used for to improve the ductility and toughness of the HfZrTi high-entropy alloy (HEAs), and why?

generation.hypothesis: Adding a moderate amount of niobium (Nb) to the HfZrTi high‐entropy alloy improves its ductility and toughness.
generation.material_initial_state: The base HfZrTi HEA, which typically exhibits limited ductility and toughness due to a relatively uniform but brittle microstructure.
generation.intervention: Introduce Nb alloying (e.g., around 5–15 at%) into the HfZrTi HEA composition.
generation.conditions: Prepare alloys under standard casting and thermomechanical treatment conditions at room temperature, ensuring controlled cooling to avoid excessive phase segregation.
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a dual-phase or refined microstructure wherein a ductile phase or grain-boundary modification is induced by Nb.
generation.mechanism: Nb is expected to lower the stacking fault energy and promote the nucleation of a more ductile phase or microstructural refinement. This dual-phase structure helps distribute strain more evenly and blunts crack propagation, thereby enhancing both ductility and toughness compared to the base alloy.
generation.predicted_outcome: The Nb-alloyed HfZrTi HEA will exhibit increased plastic deformation (higher ductility) and improved resistance to crack propagation (enhanced toughness) relative to the unmodified alloy.
generation.baseline: The original HfZrTi HEA without Nb, demonstrating lower ductility and toughness under similar processing and testing conditions.
generation.boundary: The beneficial effects are expected only within an optimal Nb concentration range. Higher Nb additions may lead to excessive formation of secondary brittle phases or undesirable segregation, nullifying the improvements.
generation.uncertainty: Moderate uncertainty exists because the optimal Nb concentration and processing conditions are not precisely known and require experimental calibration.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare a series of HfZrTi HEA samples with varying Nb contents (e.g., 0, 5, 10, and 15 at%). Process all samples under identical casting and thermomechanical treatment conditions. Characterize the microstructure using X-ray diffraction (XRD) and electron microscopy, and evaluate mechanical properties via tensile and fracture toughness tests.
measurements: Grain structure and secondary phases via SEM/TEM
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the addition of Nb does not result in a statistically significant improvement in ductility and/or toughness compared to the base HfZrTi alloy, or if the Nb-alloyed samples show an increased presence of brittle phases leading to poorer mechanical performance, then the hypothesis is falsified.
